question: Should ambiguous pre-receipt `runs.json` sources fail closed and require operator recovery, or must this PR provide a safe explicit doctor recovery path before removing runtime fallback?
rationale: Once canonical rows are empty, available state cannot reliably distinguish a stale already-imported file from a legitimate not-yet-imported file, so choosing omission risk versus resurrection risk requires explicit upgrade-policy ownership.

options.title: Add explicit recovery path
options.body: Keep fail-closed behavior by default but add a visible, verified doctor action for operators who confirm that the preserved source is authoritative.

options.title: Accept manual recovery
options.body: Land the policy as written with clear upgrade guidance that affected users must recover legitimate legacy rows manually.

options.title: Pause fallback removal
options.body: Keep the PR open until the migration can avoid both stale resurrection and legitimate-state omission without undocumented operator judgment.

recommendation.title: Add explicit recovery path
recommendation.body: Keep fail-closed behavior by default but add a visible, verified doctor action for operators who confirm that the preserved source is authoritative.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice is a shipped upgrade and recovery policy decision, and no more specific current-main history owner could be established from the available evidence.
